title: SQL Injection - Login Bypass
impact: Could allow attackers to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to user accounts or privileged application functions. Successful admin login was not confirmed.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and prepared statements. Implement secure authentication practices and avoid dynamically constructing SQL queries from user input.

title: SQL Injection - Data Extraction
impact: If successful, could allow attackers to extract sensitive database information, including user email addresses. The tested request returned No results found, so data extraction was not confirmed.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and prepared statements. Validate and sanitize user input, restrict database privileges, and avoid exposing sensitive database information.

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
impact: Could allow attackers to execute malicious JavaScript in a victim's browser through crafted links or search input, potentially leading to session theft or unauthorized actions. Successful JavaScript execution was not documented.
remediation: Apply context-aware output encoding, validate user input, implement a Content Security Policy (CSP), and avoid inserting untrusted input directly into HTML.

title: Server-Side Cross-Site Scripting Protection Bypass
url_or_endpoint: OWASP Juice Shop - Customer Feedback comment field
impact: The crafted input was accepted and the challenge success notification appeared, demonstrating a bypass of the server-side XSS protection challenge. Persistence and execution of the payload when feedback is viewed later were not established.
remediation: Validate and sanitize feedback input on the server using a well-maintained HTML sanitizer with a strict allowlist. Apply context-aware output encoding whenever feedback is displayed, and use a Content Security Policy as an additional defense.
